# Trump threatens to 'blow up' Iran as talks stall

Iran says a formal reply came days after the U.S. president called its terms unacceptable.

10/01/2026 05:50 AM EDT

U.S. President Donald Trump said Wednesday he would decide “very soon” whether to “blow up” Iran, as Tehran said it had received Washington’s formal response to its proposal to end the seven-month war.

“We have to make that decision: We blow them up or make a deal,” Trump told reporters at an Oval Office press briefing. Asked how he planned to negotiate with Iranian officials, Trump replied: “Maybe you blow them up.”

Iran’s plan, conveyed during last week’s United Nations General Assembly, called for reopening the Strait of Hormuz within a week and restarting nuclear talks. In return, Tehran wanted the U.S. to lift its naval blockade of Iranian ports, waive sanctions on Iranian oil sales and release frozen Iranian assets. Iran also called for a ceasefire on all fronts.

But Trump publicly rejected the proposal Saturday, saying Iran wanted a deal because it was “losing so badly.” He added: “They want to make a deal and I think that’s fine. I’d like to make a deal, too. But that deal would not be acceptable.”

# Iran indicates it's received an official US response to its latest offer on ending the war

Iranian officials say they have received an official U.S. response to Tehran's own proposal to end the seven-month war, which U.S. President Donald Trump rejected days earlier

ByAAMER MADHANI Associated Press

September 30, 2026, 6:59 AM

Iranian officials indicated Wednesday they have received an official U.S. response to Tehran's latest proposal to end [the seven-month war](https://apnews.com/hub/iran), which U.S. President [Donald Trump](https://apnews.com/hub/donald-trump) had publicly rejected just days earlier.

The officials did not say what the response contained and whether it was a rejection.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi presented the U.S. response to President [Masoud Pezeshkian](https://apnews.com/article/iran-pezeshkian-united-nations-general-assembly-trump-war-210d432587bb8dc2d7303ca4c8ea67b6) at a Cabinet meeting, government spokesperson Fatemeh Mohajerani told the state-run IRNA news agency.

“We will make every effort to bring the agreement to fruition and will firmly stand up for the rights of the Iranian people,” Pezeshkian said. “The agreement must now be based on a win-win strategy.”

The Cabinet meeting followed Araghchi's return to Iran after traveling to New York for last week's [U.N. General Assembly](https://apnews.com/hub/united-nations-general-assembly), where officials held [indirect talks with U.S. officials](https://apnews.com/article/trump

![Ukraine-Russia war latest: Nato responds to Putin’s nuclear weapon threat against member nations](https://imgproxy.newswav.com/665x0,q50=/https://static.independent.co.uk/2026/10/01/06/2026-09-30T175726Z_1809808932_RC2OTNA960L4_RTRMADP_3_NATO-DEFENCE-LITHUANIA-TRAINING.JPG?width=1200&auto=webp&trim=0%2C0%2C0%2C0)

Russia has sent a letter to Nato threatening to use nuclear weapons if it feels its Baltic territory of Kaliningrad is under threat.

Despite a growing campaign of Russian hybrid attacks on Ukraine's European neighbours and allies, Moscow said it was Nato exhibiting "dangerous and reckless" behaviour that entailed "high risks of the outbreak of a direct armed conflict".

The letter said Russia "will be ready to use the entire arsenal of forces and capabilities at its disposal, including nuclear weapons, in order to defend its territory".

Nato said it had responded to Moscow directly, calling on Vladimir Putin to end his invasion of Ukraine and noting “that Nato is a defensive alliance”. “We strongly denounce the threat of force, including any irresponsible nuclear rhetoric,” a spokesperson said.
